body.prompt: Friday night in a small Seoul apartment: a fried chicken delivery box just opened on a low wooden table, steam rising, a smartphone with a softly glowing screen beside it, warm lamp light, lit apartment windows of the city outside.

A narrow Korean street at dusk where several small restaurants have their metal shutters pulled down; a blank sheet of paper is taped to one shutter; a single delivery scooter passes by with its light on.

A tired fried chicken shop owner in an apron sitting on an upturned crate outside his small shop at night, a delivery rider resting on his scooter beside him; far away on the skyline a single tall glass tower glows brightly.

Seen from high above at golden hour: a single paper restaurant flyer drifting across a wide ocean, the Seoul skyline small behind it and a distant San Francisco skyline with a red suspension bridge far ahead.
A boardroom table at night with a signed contract, two fountain pens and a small toy delivery scooter in the middle; through the window a European city skyline with a tall TV tower silhouette.
Year 2020: inside an empty restaurant the chairs are stacked on the tables; through the large window, many delivery riders wearing face masks ride past at night carrying insulated boxes.
A night city seen from above where hundreds of tiny delivery scooters leave thin glowing golden trails between apartment blocks, like veins of light spreading across the city.
Close-up at an apartment door at night: a delivery rider's gloved hands hand a warm paper chicken bag to a customer, golden light spilling from inside the home.
A young owner in an apron standing proudly in front of a small newly opened fried chicken shop at night; on the counter a tablet shows incoming orders as glowing cards streaming in.
A large smartphone screen drawn as a list of restaurant cards; the top card is lifted up and shines as if paid to stay on top, small gold coins dropping from it into a jar below.
Early morning in a Seoul alley: a row of small restaurant shutters pulled down, a few lonely plastic chairs and a broom left outside, soft melancholy light.
A large franchise distribution warehouse: pallets stacked with boxes of chicken, cooking oil drums and packaging, a forklift, and a small shop owner receiving supplies at the loading dock.
Two delivery scooters racing side by side down a city street at night, each carrying an insulated box, gold coins flying off behind them as they compete.
A delivery rider in rain gear checking his phone while waiting at a red light at night, rain reflections on the wet street, an insulated delivery box on the scooter.
The classic metaphor drawn simply: a small fish about to be swallowed by a bigger fish, which is about to be swallowed by an even bigger fish, in a calm ink-wash ocean.
An old paper world map with glowing golden lines connecting the United States to Britain and then spreading across Europe and Asia, tiny delivery scooter icons travelling along the lines.
A tall glass office building on a sunny San Francisco waterfront; many faint glowing threads arrive from across the ocean and flow into the building.
A balance scale in the foreground weighing a paper chicken delivery bag against a small stack of coins; behind it, the dome of a national assembly building at dusk.
A customer at the counter of a small fried chicken shop picking up an order in person; the owner smiles while handing over the bag; warm shop light, a menu board without any text on the wall.
